chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension with chronic kidney disease and chronic pain requiring opioid therapy
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, prior myocardial infarction (2011) and stage 3 chronic kidney disease diagnosed in 2020. Since early 2020 he has persistent proteinuria and microalbuminuria despite a normal A1c (5.6%). Blood pressure remains elevated (152/110 mmHg) while on a thiazide‑ACE inhibitor combination and a low‑dose beta‑blocker. He reports chronic low‑back pain and fibromyalgia, for which he is taking high‑dose hydrocodone ER and oxycodone/acetaminophen. He works full‑time, has limited social contact, and completed higher education. Recent visits (last in September 2020) show ongoing management of hypertension, CKD, and pain but no recent labs for eGFR, lipids, or BMI.
